statement: [B-RD7: the first-level tame range] Let $p\geq5$, and permit arbitrary perfect residue fields of characteristic $p$. statement: [B-RD12: the sharp tame higher-level criterion] Fix $p\geq5$, $n\geq1$, and $m\in\{2,3,4,6\}$ with $m\mid p+1$. Assume $e$ is a positive multiple of $p-1$, and put $s=v_p(e/(p-1))$. There is a complete discretely valued $K$ of absolute ramification index $e$ and an elliptic curve with full rational $p^n$-torsion and semistability defect $m$ if and only if \[ s\geq n-1,\qquad e\geq\frac{p^2-1}{m}\, p^{\max(2n-2,\,4n-4-s)}. \tag{B.12.1} \] Arbitrary perfect residue fields are allowed; the constructions use $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$. The same assertion holds for $p=3$ with a specified tame defect $m=2$ or $4$. In that assertion no restriction on wild defects is claimed.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [B-RD13: the least good-forcing level in the tame case] Let $p\geq5$, $e\in(p-1)\mathbf Z_{>0}$, and let $m_{\max}(p)$ be as in Theorem~\ref{thm:B-RD7}. If $m_{\max}(p)e<p^2-1$, put $N=0$. Otherwise put \[ s=v_p(e/(p-1)),\qquad L=\left\lfloor\log_p\frac{m_{\max}(p)e}{p^2-1}\right\rfloor, \qquad N=1+\min\left(s,\left\lfloor\frac L2\right\rfloor, \left\lfloor\frac{L+s}{4}\right\rfloor\right). \] Among potentially good elliptic curves over all such fields of absolute ramification $e$, the least positive level $n$ at which full rational $p^n$-torsion forces good reduction is $N+1$. For $p=3$, the same formula with $m_{\max}=4$ gives the least level within the class of potentially good curves with tame inertia image.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [B-RD14: full torsion forces the cyclotomic extension] Let $A/K$ be an abelian variety of positive dimension over a characteristic-zero field. statement: [B-RD15: the unconditional reading of the least-level question] Fix $p\geq3$, a positive multiple $e$ of $p-1$, and $g\geq1$, and put $s=v_p(e/(p-1))$. Among \emph{all} abelian varieties of dimension $g$ over all complete discretely valued fields with perfect residue field and absolute ramification $e$, the least positive $n$ for which full rational $p^n$-torsion implies good reduction is $s+2$. At this level full rational $p^n$-torsion cannot occur at all. Consequently a substantive good-reduction threshold must specify the potentially good class, as in Corollary~\ref{cor:B-RD13}.

statement: [B-RD16: necessary lower bounds for character determination] Let $h\geq2$. statement: [All plane degrees in characteristic two] Let $k$ be any perfect field of characteristic two, let $U_d$ be the ordinary smooth locus in the projective space of degree-$d$ plane forms, and choose a geometric generic base point $\bar\eta$. Write \[ g=(d-1)(d-2)/2,\qquad V=H^1_{\mathrm{et}}(C_{\bar\eta},\mathbf F_2). \] For $d\ge4$, the images of $\pi_1(U_d\otimes_k\bar k,\bar\eta)$ and $\pi_1(U_d,\bar\eta)$ on $V$ are equal and are \[ \begin{cases} \mathrm{GL}_g(\mathbf F_2),&d\text{ even},\\ \operatorname{Stab}(\ell) \simeq(\mathbf F_2)^{g-1}\rtimes \mathrm{GL}_{g-1}(\mathbf F_2),&d\text{ odd}, \end{cases} \] where $\ell\ne0$ is the canonical covector determined by $\mathcal O_C((d-3)/2)\otimes B_C^{-1}$ in odd degree. The nonzero representation is irreducible exactly in even degree; its determinant is always trivial. In degrees one and two $V=0$; in degree three it has rank one and trivial, hence irreducible, monodromy. Thus there is no threshold after which all plane degrees have full linear or irreducible monodromy.

statement: [A differential subring with an analytically ramified completion] Let $V$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ with uniformizer $p$, fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$. Let $C\subset K$ be a subfield such that $C\cap V\to k$ is onto. Let $J\in V$ be transcendental over $C$, let $F\subset K$ be an algebraic extension of $C(J)$, and let $D:F\to F$ extend the derivation which is zero on $C$ and sends $J$ to $1$. Put \[ V_0=F\cap V,\qquad R=\{a\in V_0:D(a)\in V_0\}. \] Then $R$ is a one-dimensional noetherian local domain, with fraction field $F$ and residue field $k$. Its normalization is the DVR $V_0$, which has uniformizer $p$ and residue field $k$; both the fraction-field and residue-field extensions induced by $R\subset V_0$ are identities. In particular $R$ is geometrically unibranch. Its normalization is not finite, and the homomorphism \[ R\longrightarrow V[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2), \qquad a\longmapsto a+\epsilon D(a) \tag{C-RD11.1} \] identifies its maximal-ideal completion with $V[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$.

statement: [C-RD1: proper epimorphisms] Let $S$ be a noetherian scheme, let $f:S'\to S$ be proper, and suppose $\mathcal O_S\to f_*\mathcal O_{S'}$ is injective. Put $S''=S'\times_S S'$. statement: [Refutation of full linear monodromy] For every finite field of characteristic two and every odd $d\geq5$, let $\bar\eta$ be a geometric generic point of the ordinary smooth degree-$d$ plane-curve locus $U_d$, and put $V=H^1_{\mathrm{et}}(C_{\bar\eta},\mathbf F_2)$. Both images \[ G_{\mathrm{geom}}=\mathrm{im}\bigl(\pi_1(U_d\otimes\bar k,\bar\eta) \to\mathrm{GL}(V)\bigr),\qquad G_{\mathrm{arith}}=\mathrm{im}\bigl(\pi_1(U_d,\bar\eta) \to\mathrm{GL}(V)\bigr) \] fix a nonzero covector. Consequently both are contained in the proper subgroup \[ \mathrm{Stab}(\ell)\simeq \mathbf F_2^{\,g_d-1}\rtimes\mathrm{GL}_{g_d-1}(\mathbf F_2), \] and $V$ is reducible, with invariant hyperplane $\ker\ell$. There is no integer $d_1(\mathbf P^2)$ for which the proposed full linear geometric or arithmetic monodromy holds for every $d\geq d_1$ in characteristic two.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $k$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$. For every $d\geq4$, every nonempty Zariski open $U\subset S_d$, and every $a\in\mathbf F_p$, there exist a finite extension $k'/k$ and a smooth plane curve $C\in U(k')$ of degree $d$ with $\#C(k')\equiv a\pmod p$. For $d=1,2$ the only residue for smooth curves is $1$. For $d=3$, the residues on the ordinary smooth locus are exactly $\mathbf F_p\setminus\{1\}$, and every nonempty open of that locus attains every such residue after a finite extension. Supersingular smooth cubics give residue $1$, so all residues occur among all smooth cubics; the every-open assertion for all residues fails in degree three.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: For every $d\geq d_0$, the generic smooth hypersurface section $Y$ of degree $d$ has $\dim E(Y,\mathcal O_Y)_{\mathrm{ss}}>0$. More precisely, for every $d\geq\max\{1,r_\omega-1\}$, its generic rank $f_{X,d}$ satisfies \begin{equation} f_{X,d}\ \geq\ D\binom dn-D\binom d{n-1} -\sum_{m=1}^{n-2}B_m\binom dm-a, \end{equation} where a binomial coefficient with lower index greater than $d$ is zero. Consequently \[ f_{X,d}=\frac{D}{n!}d^n+O_X(d^{n-1})\quad(d\longrightarrow\infty). \]
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [The eventual parenthesis of 8.5.8] For the explicit $d_0$ of \eqref{eq:explicit-d0}, every $d\geq d_0$ has the following properties. Every smooth degree-$d$ section $Y$ satisfies \[ \dim E(Y,\mathcal O_Y) =h^0(X,\omega_X\otimes L^d)-h^0(X,\omega_X)>0. \] For every $Y$ in the maximal-stable-rank open $U_d$, the number of $p$-adic unit roots in vanishing cohomology is positive. Thus, on this open and in this stated eventual range, unit-root nonvanishing and the maximal Hodge-level condition $E(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\ne0$ are equivalent. No assumption on crystalline $p$-torsion of $X$ is needed.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $k$ be finite of characteristic $p$, let $n\geq2$, and let $d\geq pn+1$. Every nonempty open in the degree-$d$ hypersurface parameter space of $\mathbf P^n_k$ contains, over a finite extension, a smooth hypersurface with any prescribed point-count residue modulo $p$.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $G$ be a finite commutative group scheme over a field $k$, and let $Z\to X$ be a $G$-torsor, where $Z$ is a positive dimensional projective complete intersection of dimension at least two and $X$ is smooth and geometrically connected. If $G^D$ is connected, then \[ \operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}^0=G^D. \]
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: For the fixed smooth projective geometrically connected surface $(X,L)/k$ just constructed, let $r_\omega$ be a regularity bound for its embedded dualizing sheaf, and put $d_* =\max\{1,r_\omega-1\}$. For every $d\geq d_*$ and every smooth section $Y\in|L^d|$, of genus $g_Y$, one has \[ \dim E(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=g_Y-1, \qquad \dim E(Y,\mathcal O_Y)_{\mathrm{ss}} =f_Y\leq g_Y-2, \] where $f_Y$ is the $2$-rank of its Jacobian. In particular the Frobenius on $E(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ is never bijective in this entire range, including at the generic point.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: For the universal ordinary smooth plane quintic in characteristic two, the geometric and arithmetic monodromy groups on $V=H^1_{\mathrm{et}}(C_{\bar\eta},\mathbf F_2)$ are both the full stabilizer of the canonical nonzero covector: \[ G_{\mathrm{geom}}=G_{\mathrm{arith}} =\operatorname{Stab}_{\mathrm{GL}_6(\mathbf F_2)}(\ell) \simeq\mathbf F_2^5\rtimes\mathrm{GL}_5(\mathbf F_2). \] In particular their order is $319979520$, the representation is reducible with invariant hyperplane of dimension five, and the determinant character is trivial.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: For the universal ordinary smooth plane sextic in characteristic two, the geometric and arithmetic monodromy images on $V=H^1_{\mathrm{et}}(C_{\bar\eta},\mathbf F_2)$ are both $\mathrm{GL}_{10}(\mathbf F_2)$. Thus $V$ is irreducible and its determinant character is trivial.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: For the universal ordinary smooth plane septic in characteristic two, the geometric and arithmetic monodromy images on $V=H^1_{\mathrm{et}}(C_{\bar\eta},\mathbf F_2)$ are the full stabilizer of the distinguished nonzero covector supplied by $\mathcal O_C(2)$ and the canonical theta characteristic: \[ G_{\mathrm{geom}}=G_{\mathrm{arith}} =\operatorname{Stab}(\ell) \simeq 2^{14}\!:\mathrm{GL}_{14}(\mathbf F_2). \] In particular, the rank-fifteen representation is reducible, with its distinguished invariant hyperplane, and its determinant is trivial.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [The conductor inclusion for an even contact] Let $C$ be a smooth plane curve of degree $d$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two, and let $Q$ be a reduced plane curve of degree $s<d$ with $Q\cap C=2D$ as divisors on $C$. Write $\nu:\widetilde Q=\coprod Q_i\to Q$ for the normalization, and write \[ \operatorname{div}(f|_{Q_i})=2A_i+\epsilon_i, \qquad M_i=\mathcal O_{Q_i}(A_i), \] where $f$ defines $C$ and $\epsilon_i$ is the reduced odd-order divisor. It is supported above the singular points of $Q$. Set \[ J=\mathcal I_{D/Q}(s),\qquad L_C=\mathcal O_C(D),\qquad b=d-s. \] Then \begin{equation} h^0(C,L_C)=1+h^0(Q,J), \end{equation} and there is an inclusion \begin{equation} \nu_*\left(\bigoplus_i \omega_{Q_i}\otimes M_i^{-1}(3)\right)\hookrightarrow J. \end{equation} In particular, with $t=\sum_i h^1(Q_i,M_i)$, \begin{equation} h^0(Q,J)\ge t, \qquad t>0\Longrightarrow h^0(Q,J)\ge t+1. \end{equation}
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [No lower-degree reduced contact for a generic curve] Fix $d\ge4$ and $0<s<d-3$ in characteristic two. A generic smooth plane curve $C$ of degree $d$ has no reduced plane curve $Q$ of degree $s$ with $Q|C$ even.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [The theta orbits of generic plane curves in characteristic two] Let $d\ge4$, $g=(d-1)(d-2)/2$, and let $C$ be the geometric generic ordinary smooth plane curve of degree $d$ in characteristic two. If $d$ is even, every theta characteristic other than the canonical one $B_C$ has exactly one section, and geometric monodromy is transitive on these $2^g-1$ characteristics. If $d$ is odd, every theta characteristic other than $B_C$ and $\mathcal O_C((d-3)/2)$ has exactly one section, and geometric monodromy is transitive on these $2^g-2$ characteristics. Equivalently, on $V^\vee$ geometric monodromy is transitive on all nonzero vectors in even degree, and on $V^\vee\setminus\{0,v\}$ in odd degree, where $v$ is the distinguished nonzero invariant vector.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Every nonzero $S_d$-submodule of $\bigwedge^2W$ contains $A$. If $p\nmid d$, then $A=V$ and $V$ is simple. If $p\mid d$, then $A$ is the unique proper nonzero submodule, and $V/A\simeq D$ is simple of dimension $d-2$.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: The geometric monodromy group $G$ is irreducible on $V$.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: For every odd prime $p$, the natural three-dimensional module $Q$ and its dual satisfy $H^1(\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbf F_p),Q)= H^1(\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbf F_p),Q^*)=0$.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let an irreducible finite group $G\subseteq\mathrm{GL}(V)$ contain a transvection, and let $N\triangleleft G$ be the subgroup generated by all transvections in $G$. Then $V$ is a direct sum of pairwise nonisomorphic simple $N$-modules, and $G$ permutes these summands transitively. Every transvection has its image line in exactly one summand and fixes all the others pointwise.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: The normal subgroup $N\triangleleft G$ generated by all transvections is irreducible on $V$.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $p$ be odd and let $U_d$ be the ordinary smooth plane-curve locus of degree $d$ over any perfect field $k$ of characteristic $p$. At a geometric generic point put $V=H^1_{\mathrm{et}}(C_{\bar\eta},\mathbf F_p)$, of dimension $g=(d-1)(d-2)/2$. For every $d\geq3$, both the geometric and the arithmetic monodromy images on $V$ are $\mathrm{GL}_g(\mathbf F_p)$, with full determinant character. For $d=1,2$ both images are trivial on the zero vector space. For positive rank the representation is irreducible.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $U$ be a nonempty open in $\mathbf P^N_k$, and let $T\to U$ be a connected finite etale cover. Let $f:\mathbf P^N\dashrightarrow\mathbf P^M$ be a linear projection whose center $Z$ meets $U$. The restriction of $T$ to the geometric generic fibre of $f|_{U\setminus Z}$ is connected. Consequently a finite local system on $U$ retains its full monodromy after restriction to that geometric generic fibre.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: For $e\geq n+1$, fix a hyperplane $H\subset\mathbf P^n$. The local system $V_{n,e}$ retains its full geometric monodromy when the restriction of the equation to $H$ is prescribed to be geometric generic. On the parameter space where both the equation and its restriction have invertible Hasse--Witt maps, the joint monodromy image on $V_{n,e}$ and $V_{n-1,e}$ is the product of their two full images.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Assume $1\leq n\leq d-2$. If $p\nmid d$, then $\bigwedge^nW$ is simple as an $S_d$-module. If $p\mid d$, then $A=\bigwedge^nD$ is its unique proper nonzero submodule; both $A$ and the quotient $\bigwedge^{n-1}D$ are simple.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: For $n\geq2$ and $d\geq n+2$, the geometric group on $V_{n,d}$ contains commuting rank-one reflections $R_I$, indexed by $(n-1)$-subsets $I\subset\{3,\ldots,d\}$. At the arrangement base point, their negative eigenlines are \[ \left\langle (e_1-e_2)\wedge\bigwedge_{i\in I}e_i\right\rangle, \] and their product is the permutation transposition $(12)$. Here a rank-one reflection has eigenvalue $-1$ once and eigenvalue $1$ on a codimension-one subspace.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: For $n\geq2$ and $d\geq n+2$, the geometric monodromy group $G_{n,d}$ is irreducible.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: For $n\geq3$ and $d=n+2$, the group $G_{n,d}$ contains $\mathrm{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbf F_p)$.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: If an irreducible normal subgroup $N\triangleleft G$ is the natural symplectic group in dimension $h\geq3$ over an odd prime field, then $G$ cannot contain a rank-one reflection.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Suppose the groups for degree $d-1$ in $\mathbf P^n$ and $\mathbf P^{n-1}$ contain their full special linear groups, where $n\geq3$ and $d\geq n+3$. Then $G_{n,d}$ contains $\mathrm{SL}_{h_{n,d}}(\mathbf F_p)$. If in addition the first of these two groups has full determinant, then so does $G_{n,d}$.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: There is a family of plane cubics over a strictly henselian smooth trait over $k$ whose special fibre is smooth supersingular, whose Hasse invariant has valuation one, and whose restriction to a fixed line is the constant squarefree binary cubic $g=x_0x_1(x_0-x_1)$. There are also smooth ordinary plane cubics with this same restriction.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: For every $n\geq2$, the geometric determinant images in degrees $n+1$ and $n+2$ are the full group $\mathbf F_p^\times$.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $p$ be odd, let $k$ be any perfect field of characteristic $p$, and let $n\geq2$. On the ordinary smooth degree-$d$ hypersurface locus in $\mathbf P^n_k$, the geometric and arithmetic monodromy images on $H^{n-1}_{\mathrm{et}}(Y_{\bar\eta},\mathbf F_p)$ are both \[ \mathrm{GL}_{\binom{d-1}{n}}(\mathbf F_p). \] For $d\leq n$ the vector space is zero and the image is trivial. For $d=n+1$ it has rank one and full determinant. For every $d\geq n+2$ it is irreducible with full determinant.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $k$ be finite of odd characteristic $p$ and $n\geq2$. For every $d\geq n+2$, every nonempty open in the smooth degree-$d$ hypersurface locus of $\mathbf P^n_k$ contains, over suitable finite extensions of $k$, hypersurfaces with each of the $p$ point-count residues. For $d\leq n$ every smooth hypersurface has residue $1$. For $d=n+1$ the ordinary open misses residue $1$. Thus $d=n+2$ is the exact threshold for the assertion involving every nonempty open.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: The geometric monodromy contains, for each $(n-1)$-subset $I\subset\{2,\ldots,m\}$, the transvection \begin{equation} R_I=1+w_I\phi_I,\qquad w_I=\sum_{\substack{a\in\{2,\ldots,m\}\\a\notin I}}b_{I\cup\{a\}}, \quad \phi_I=b_{\{1\}\cup I}^*. \end{equation} It fixes every exterior basis vector except $b_{\{1\}\cup I}$, which it sends to $\sum_{a\notin I}b_{I\cup\{a\}}$. The swaps for different $I$ are independent monodromy elements.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $G_0$ be generated by the arrangement permutation group and the swaps of Lemma~\ref{lem:char2-independent-quadric-swaps}. Writing $\ell=\sum_A b_A^*$, one has \[ G_0= \begin{cases} \mathrm{GL}_{h}(\mathbf F_2),&d-n-1\ \text{odd},\\ \operatorname{Stab}_{\mathrm{GL}_h(\mathbf F_2)}(\ell), &d-n-1\ \text{even}. \end{cases} \] In the second case the stabilizer is $\mathbf F_2^{h-1}\rtimes\mathrm{GL}_{h-1}(\mathbf F_2)$.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: If $d\equiv n+1\pmod2$ and $d\geq n+1$, the universal ordinary Hasse--Witt local system has a nowhere-zero invariant $\mathbf F_2$-valued covector, defined over $\mathbf F_2$.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $k$ be any perfect field of characteristic two and $n\geq2$. Put $h=\binom{d-1}{n}$. The geometric and arithmetic monodromy groups on the ordinary smooth degree-$d$ hypersurface locus of $\mathbf P^n_k$ are: \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{degree range}&\text{both monodromy images}\\ \hline d\leq n&1\text{ on the zero vector space}\\ d=n+1&\mathrm{GL}_1(\mathbf F_2)=1\\ d\geq n+2,\ d\equiv n\pmod2&\mathrm{GL}_h(\mathbf F_2)\\ d\geq n+3,\ d\equiv n+1\pmod2& \operatorname{Stab}(\lambda) \simeq\mathbf F_2^{h-1}\rtimes \mathrm{GL}_{h-1}(\mathbf F_2), \end{array} \] where $\lambda$ is the nonzero covector in Lemma~\ref{lem:pn-char2-canonical-covector}. In the last case $\ker\lambda$ is a proper nonzero invariant hyperplane, so the representation is reducible.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: For every finite field $k$, every $n\geq2$, and every $d\geq n+2$, each nonempty open in the smooth degree-$d$ hypersurface parameter space of $\mathbf P^n_k$ contains hypersurfaces, over suitable finite extensions of $k$, with every point-count residue modulo the characteristic. The threshold $n+2$ is exact: for $d\leq n$ the only residue is $1$, and for $d=n+1$ the ordinary open misses $1$.
notes: Proof incorporated; targeted audit state in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.
